description: VECTOR_SUM - every expectation measured on a real Snowflake account. It sums ELEMENT-WISE, skipping NULL rows, and reduces each dimension INDEPENDENTLY: the cross-row fixture is chosen so no row is the winner everywhere, giving [12.000000,16.000000,-3.000000]. The element type is NOT widened to FLOAT, so an INT input sums to [5,14,-3]. A group with no non-NULL row is SQL NULL, not a zero vector; a single-row group is that row; GROUP BY keeps per-group results, including NULL for the NULL row's own group. A non-vector argument is a compile error naming the argument's type. Converted 1:1 from functions/vector/VectorSumTest (now retired); every vector is read as a bare cell, as recorded in functions-vector-avg. The Java's grouped test read row indexes out of a ResultSet; the converted test asserts the whole grouped column as one ordered row set instead.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sum_rows (id INTEGER, v VECTOR(FLOAT,3))
CREATE TABLE sum_rows (id INTEGER, v VECTOR(FLOAT,3))
SELECT VECTOR_SUM(v) FROM sum_rows WHERE id = 99
SELECT VECTOR_SUM(v) FROM sum_rows WHERE id = 3
CREATE TABLE sum_rows (id INTEGER, v VECTOR(FLOAT,3))
SELECT VECTOR_SUM(v) FROM sum_rows WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE sum_rows (id INTEGER, v VECTOR(FLOAT,3))
SELECT id, VECTOR_SUM(v) FROM sum_rows GROUP BY id ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE sum_rows (id INTEGER, v VECTOR(FLOAT,3))
